guide: Build and launch a travel app where people keep a profile of places they have been and collect a stamp for each one; you need an AI coding assistant (ChatGPT / Codex or Claude Code), a free Supabase account and a free Vercel account.
1. Write down the core idea in two sentences: who the app is for, and the one thing they do (here, log a place and collect a stamp for it).
1. Ask Claude Code or Codex to scaffold a Next.js app with a profile page, a "places I've been" list and a stamp for each place.
1. Create a Supabase project and add tables for users, places and stamps, with sign-in switched on.
1. Connect the app to Supabase using the project URL and public key, and keep any secret keys out of the code.
1. Make a mock version first with sample photos and fake data so you can see how the profile and stamps look before real users arrive.
1. Record a short screen video of the mock walking through the profile, the places and the stamps, so you can show people what it does.
1. Deploy the app to Vercel from your Git repository and test sign-up on your phone.
1. Open it to your first users and post the video with the link.
Watch out: the video used mock data and stock-style pictures, so say plainly that it is a demo, and never put real users' details or photos in a recording.

```
You are a senior full-stack developer. Build a simple travel-passport web app called <app name> for <target audience>. Users sign up, build a profile, add places they have visited with a photo and date, and receive a visual stamp for each place, shown on their profile. I have a <ChatGPT/Codex or Claude Code> account, a free Supabase account and a free Vercel account, and I am a beginner, so explain each step briefly. Use Next.js for the front end, Supabase for sign-in, the database and photo storage, and deploy to Vercel. Create the database tables and row-level security so each user can only edit their own data. Add a seed script with clearly fake sample data so I can record a demo. Keep secret keys in environment variables and never in the code. Return the project structure, the SQL for the tables, the key files, and a short checklist for deploying and testing sign-up on a phone. Ask me up to three questions first if anything is unclear.
```
